questions.stem: Which of the following is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet — its mass (~1.9×10²⁷ kg) is more than twice the mass of all other planets in the solar system combined. Its diameter (~140,000 km) is about 11 times Earth's. Saturn is second-largest. Neptune is smaller than both but denser than Saturn. Earth is the fifth-largest planet.

questions.stem: Which planet is known as the 'Morning Star' and the 'Evening Star'?
questions.explanation: Venus is visible shortly before sunrise (Morning Star) or shortly after sunset (Evening Star) because its orbit lies INSIDE Earth's — meaning it can never be seen at midnight. Its thick sulfuric-acid clouds reflect ~70% of sunlight, making it the 2nd-brightest natural object in the night sky after the Moon. Mercury also has 'Morning Star'/'Evening Star' visibility but is much dimmer and harder to spot.

questions.stem: Which planet has the most number of moons (as of 2024)?
questions.explanation: As of 2024, Saturn has ~146 confirmed moons (after a 2023 announcement added 62 new moons), surpassing Jupiter's ~95. Titan is Saturn's largest moon (larger than the planet Mercury) and has a thick atmosphere. Jupiter's Galilean moons (Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto) are the most famous. Counts change over time as new small moons are discovered; exam answers use current NASA-certified counts.

questions.stem: Why is Mercury the hottest planet during the day but not on average?

options.option_text: Because it rotates very slowly, but has no atmosphere to retain heat at night
Because its orbit is elliptical and it is sometimes very far from the Sun
Because it has thick clouds that reflect heat away
Because it is made of ice

questions.explanation: Mercury has virtually NO atmosphere (exosphere only). So during the day, its surface reaches ~430°C (closer to Sun). At night, without any atmosphere to retain heat, temperatures plunge to ~−180°C. VENUS, despite being farther from the Sun, is the HOTTEST planet on average (surface ~465°C) due to its extreme CO₂ greenhouse effect. Mercury has very slow rotation (1 Mercury-day = 59 Earth-days) exposing each side to extreme temperatures.

questions.stem: Which of these planets does NOT have a ring system?
questions.explanation: All four GAS/ICE GIANTS (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) have ring systems. Saturn's rings are the most visible and extensive (made mostly of water ice). Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune have fainter rings. Earth — a terrestrial planet — has NO rings. Among dwarf planets, Haumea and the centaur Chariklo also have confirmed rings. Mars and Venus have no rings either.

questions.stem: When and why was Pluto reclassified as a 'dwarf planet'?

options.option_text: In 2006 by IAU, because it failed to clear its orbital neighborhood of other objects
In 1990 by NASA, because Voyager-2 found no atmosphere
In 2012 by UN Space Committee, because of its small size alone
In 2019 by Hubble Space Telescope, because of its elliptical orbit

questions.explanation: In August 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) established three criteria for PLANET status: (1) orbits the Sun; (2) sufficient mass for hydrostatic equilibrium (spherical); (3) has cleared the neighborhood around its orbit. Pluto satisfies (1) and (2) but NOT (3) — its orbit is dominated by other Kuiper Belt objects, some larger than Pluto (e.g., Eris). It was thus reclassified as a 'dwarf planet'. Other dwarf planets: Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Ceres.

questions.stem: Which planet has a day (rotation) longer than its year (revolution)?
questions.explanation: Venus's rotation period (sidereal day) is ~243 Earth-days, while its orbital period (year) is ~225 Earth-days. So a VENUSIAN DAY is LONGER than a VENUSIAN YEAR! Venus also rotates RETROGRADE (opposite to most planets) — meaning the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east on Venus. Mercury has a day of 59 Earth-days and year of 88 Earth-days (day < year).

questions.stem: The asteroid belt in our solar system lies between which two planets?
questions.explanation: The main ASTEROID BELT lies between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, at ~2.2–3.2 AU from the Sun. It contains millions of rocky bodies, the largest being Ceres (a dwarf planet). Jupiter's gravity prevented material in this region from coalescing into a planet. The KUIPER BELT (beyond Neptune) is a separate belt of icy bodies and the OORT CLOUD is a spherical shell of comets far beyond.

questions.stem: Which planet tilts on its side (axial tilt ~98°), causing extreme seasonal variations?
questions.explanation: Uranus's axial tilt is ~98°, meaning its rotation axis is nearly in the plane of its orbit. As a result, each pole receives ~42 years of continuous sunlight followed by ~42 years of darkness — extreme seasons. Hypothesis: a massive early collision may have knocked Uranus on its side. Earth's tilt is 23.5°; Mars 25°; Saturn 27°; Neptune 28°.
